transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-14
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Leah Morrison (Seabreeze - Head of Data Governance), Tom Baird (Platform Eng), Aisha Rahman (Compliance)

Auto-generated summary: Discussed residency constraints across EU and US, keystore routing for customer-managed keys, log retention/redaction needs and final evidence artifacts required for audit. Agreed to pilot with region-locked Private deployment and a keystore routing POC.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, uh this is Maya from Redwood Inference, joining with Diego on the tech side. how's everyone doing?
[00:07] Leah: good thanks, been looking forward to this. we had a couple internal kickoff notes but we wanted to run through constraints first.
[00:12] Tom: yep, i'll jump in on infra questions. aisha will cover compliance.
[00:16] Aisha: hi all, thanks.
[00:18] Diego: great. quick agenda - residency requirements, keystore/KMS routing, logs & evidence, and pilot scope. sound ok?
[00:24] Leah: yes, let's start with residency. we have EU-resident customer data that cannot leave EU regions, also some US-regulated data that must stay in us-east. we may have different datasets with different controls.
[00:36] Maya: understood. do you currently host models on-prem or in cloud? and are you running inference in production yet?
[00:43] Tom: right now we call a mix - internal models in our VPC in GCP europe-west1 and some 3rd party inference is in a managed endpoint. performance isn't great on peak.
[00:52] Diego: ok, makes sense. for the residency case we usually present three paths - Redwood Hosted where we can regionalize endpoints, Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity in a region/zone), and Redwood Private which is private control plane + customer VPC / on-prem option.
[01:05] Aisha: can you guarantee geofencing? like lock a model to EU so keys and logs never leave EU?
[01:10] Maya: yes, we can do region-locking for both data plane and logs in Private and Dedicated modes. Hosted can be region-specific too but the control plane metadata might flow to our US control plane unless we run a private control plane.
[01:22] Leah: that's the key - we need control plane evidence to show to auditors. SSO logs, change history, who triggered model rollouts.
[01:29] Diego: for that, Private gives you the easiest path: you run the control plane inside your VPC, we provide the customer managed images and you keep the keystore keys in your KMS. we support KMS/HSM integrations and you can configure routing rules so any KMS calls never leave your region.
[01:44] Tom: wait, when you say "keystore routing rules" are we talking about pulling data into Redwood or can we route requests back to our KMS?
[01:51] Diego: you can route. architecture is: model runtime fetches a key reference, but key operations (sign/decrypt) can be proxied to your KMS — so the private deployment keeps ephemeral keys local. some customers also use HSM-backed KMS in their cloud account.
[02:06] Leah: good. for audit we also need attestation that keys are customer-owned and that logs aren't stored outside EU. do you provide an attestation doc?
[02:15] Maya: we can provide SOC 2 type II report and a keystore-residency attestation template; we'll share the security pack after the call.
[02:23] Aisha: what about redaction? we cannot store raw PII in logs. can Redwood do automatic redaction before logs are persisted?
[02:31] Diego: we have streaming hooks where you can apply regex redaction or pass logs through your sanitizer. in Private you can host that pipeline; in Hosted we offer configurable redaction but for strict regulated PII we recommend Private so you control the sanitizers.
[02:47] Tom: and retention windows? auditors want 7 years of some records but we have a mix. is retention configurable per stream?
[02:55] Maya: yes, retention is configurable per-log stream. you can set different retention for trace vs. request/body vs. raw-model-ops. note though long retention has cost and storage implications.
[03:07] Leah: also need to know access patterns - who from Redwood ops can see logs? we are sensitive about vendor access.
[03:13] Diego: in Private deployments you can elect to disable vendor SRE access entirely; for Dedicated we can offer role-based access and strict jumpbox policies subject to contract.
[03:23] Aisha: does Redwood support SAML SSO + SCIM for user provisioning? that's non-negotiable for our security team.
[03:29] Maya: yes, SAML + SCIM yes, RBAC configurable per-team, and audit logs for admin actions.
[03:35] Tom: technical deep dive - latency is a concern, we run low-latency scoring (under 100ms p95). how does Private compare vs Dedicated performance-wise?
[03:45] Diego: performance is mostly determined by hardware and kernel optimizations. Dedicated gives you optimized GPU pools for predictable latency; Private can match if you deploy on identical hardware in your VPC. Hosted may have more variance unless you reserve capacity.
[03:59] Leah: procurement question - we're prioritizing solutions we can evidence in a security review by end of quarter, is a pilot acceptable?
[04:06] Maya: yes, most customers do a pilot: we typically run a short POC with a subset of data and a residency-locked model endpoint.
[04:12] Aisha: what evidence will you provide during pilot? we need sample audit logs, keystore usage logs, and a runbook of the deployment steps.
[04:19] Diego: we'll provide access to an evidence bundle: sample logs (with redaction), control plane audit trail, and a keystore routing demo showing KMS calls logged in-region.
[04:28] Tom: how do you handle dual residency? e.g., an inference request that needs EU model but US dataset — in theory shouldn't happen but in microservices flows it can.
[04:39] Diego: you set routing rules: requests tagged with EU dataset go to EU model endpoints. we support request tagging and header-based routing at the gateway level.
[04:48] Leah: ok that helps. one other constraint — legal wants to know about subprocessor list. do you publish a subprocessors registry?
[04:55] Maya: yes, subprocessors list is in the security pack; for Private we can exclude certain subprocessors since you control the infra.
[05:03] Aisha: cross-border fallback: if EU zone is down, what's the behavior? our legal wants a fail closed vs fail open discussion.
[05:11] Diego: we support failover policies. you can configure strict fail-closed for some datasets (reject if region unavailable) or allow degraded fallback to another region with an audit event. auditors usually prefer fail-closed for high-risk data.
[05:24] Tom: and if we need encryption key escrow for long-term access post-contract?
[05:30] Maya: we support keystore export/escrow workflows; we'd coordinate with your security team for transfer and attestations.
[05:37] Leah: timeline — we're targeting an internal vendor review by 09/30 and procurement by 11/01. pilot ideally done by end of July so security can test.
[05:46] Maya: ok we can aim to kick off pilot week of 2026-07-27. we'll share a pilot template and required inputs.
[05:52] Aisha: can we see sample runbook steps so security can pre-clear them?
[05:58] Diego: yes, i'll draft a runbook with commands and required network rules and share.
[06:03] Maya: to be explicit on scope: pilot will validate keystore routing, log redaction and retention, and control plane audit evidence. we'll keep it limited to a single model and a small dataset.
[06:14] Leah: that aligns. any blockers on our side? we need to enumerate data classes and approve network peering.
[06:20] Tom: we'll need a list of required firewall rules and NAT egress rules for the POC.
[06:25] Diego: noted, i'll include an egress/peering checklist.
[06:28] Maya: curious — have you evaluated Anthropic or Bedrock?
[06:31] Leah: we've done some higher-level evals; Bedrock was attractive for integration with other AWS tooling but we couldn't find a clean path for private keystore ownership. Anthropic was promising but hosting controls were limited.
[06:43] Maya: ok that's helpful. pricing question - Dedicated vs Private delta?
[06:47] Maya: generally Private has a platform fee + infra costs since you're running the control plane; Dedicated is managed infra with reserved capacity pricing. we'll send a templated cost comparison.
[06:57] Tom: can we run the control plane in our VPC but have Redwood manage the images/upgrades? we want to avoid daily ops but still control the network.
[07:05] Diego: yes, that's a common hybrid: customer-managed control plane with optional Redwood-managed updates under strict change windows and signed artifacts.
[07:14] Leah: legal question — do you support contractual clauses for data residency guarantees and audit rights?
[07:21] Maya: yes we have contractual language for residency guarantees and audit rights included in enterprise agreements; we'll work with legal to scope.
[07:28] Aisha: ok, one more technical - log redaction accuracy. can you do NLP-based PII detection instead of regex?
[07:36] Diego: we have both; regex for deterministic fields and ML-based PII scrubbers for unstructured text. for regulated cases we recommend a hybrid approach and customer review.
[07:47] Tom: network-wise, will Private require us to open inbound ports? we prefer outbound-only connections through a peered VPC.
[07:55] Diego: Private supports outbound-only peering; we can use NAT and private peering. inbound opening is optional only for certain debugging flows.
[08:05] Leah: great. that's a lot. can we recap next steps?
[08:09] Maya: sure - i'll share security pack + SOC2 + keystore attestation template by Friday (2026-07-17). Diego will share runbook, keystore routing diagram, and POC config by Monday (2026-07-20). Leah will share data class list and compliance checklist by 2026-07-21. we'll target pilot kickoff week of 2026-07-27.
[08:28] Tom: sounds good. anything else?
[08:30] Aisha: just to record - we want fail-closed as default for EU-resident PII in pilot.
[08:36] Diego: noted, will configure that in demo.
[08:38] Maya: ok thanks everyone. we'll follow up with calendar invite and a short intake form.
[08:44] Leah: thanks all.
[08:46] (meeting ends)
